claims.text:
The name is not explained, however in The Etymologies, the name-element -dor (a compounded form of Noldorin taur) has the sense of "king, master".
It has been suggested that the first element of the name could be gwind "pale blue".
It has been suggested by Paul Strack and David Salo that the Gwindor is a Sindarin name could be derived from a combination of the elements gwain ("new") + -dor ("lord").
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lost Road and Other Writings, Part Three: "The Etymologies", entry"TA", "TA3"; citing J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lost Road and Other Writings, Part Three: "The Etymologies", entry"WIN"

claims.text: During the assault, Gwindor led a small company of Elves of Nargothrond stationed at Barad Eithel. But the hosts of Morgoth were prepared; they brought his brother, still alive, then mutilated and slew him in front of the company. At the sight of Gelmir's mangled corpse, he charged on the plains of Anfauglith, and thus beginning the battle of Nirnaeth Arnoediad. It is said that Morgoth trembled as his company pounded on his gates, but he had ambushed the company within Angband itself, and all but Gwindor were slain.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of the Fifth Battle: Nirnaeth Arnoediad"
claims.section: section == History == > Battle of Unnumbered Tears and thralldom

claims.text: He spent fourteen years as a captive slave in Angband where the strength and beauty of his body were ruined. At some point, he received a small sword from another Elf who worked in the forges and, while working in a stone-gang, turned suddenly on the guards. Though he lost a hand in that fight, he managed to escape and fled southwards, eventually reaching Taur-nu-Fuin.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Children of Húrin, "The Death of Beleg"
claims.section: section == History == > Battle of Unnumbered Tears and thralldom

claims.text: Gwindor was born in Nargothrond to Guilin and was the brother of Gelmir. He was considered a bold leader, and the scout who scoured most far afield of all the folk of Nargothrond. He was betrothed to Finduilas the daughter of Orodreth.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Children of Húrin, "The Death of Beleg", p. 157; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lays of Beleriand, "I. The Lay of the Children of Húrin: III. Failivrin"

claims.text: Indeed, Gwindor was right and Glaurung with a band of Orcs came. The Elves were driven towards the plain of Tumhalad, where most of them, including King Orodreth and Gwindor, were slain in battle. Before dying, he assigned the protection of Finduilas to Túrin, and informed him that she alone could save him from the Curse of Morgoth; however his warning was not heeded, as Túrin failed to protect her.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of Túrin Turambar"

claims.text: In Turambar and the Foalókë, he is initially named Flinding, son of Duilin, and serves the same role as an escaped thrall of Melko who assists in rescuing Túrin and eventually guiding him to the caves of the Rodothlim.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "II. Turambar and the Foalókë"
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Book of Lost Tales

claims.text: There is no relation stated between him and Failivrin, daughter of Galweg, who would become Finduilas.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "II. Turambar and the Foalókë"
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Book of Lost Tales

claims.text: Flinding was only lightly injured during the pitched battle with the Orcs (what would become the Battle of Tumhalad), and aided Túrin in carrying the mortally wounded Orodreth back to the caves. He then stood beside Túrin in protecting the dwelling of Galweg from the ransacking Orcs until he was felled by an arrow to the eye.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Book of Lost Tales Part Two, "II. Turambar and the Foalókë"
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Book of Lost Tales

claims.text: In The Earliest Annals of Beleriand he is renamed to Findor son of Fuilin, and then a final time to Gwindor son of Guilin.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Shaping of Middle-earth, "VII. The Earliest Annals of Beleriand: Notes [to text AB I]", p. 312, note 40
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Later works

claims.text: Beleg insisted that Flinding show him the way to the Orc camp, which Flinding initially declined, stating that fear fettered him, and he would prefer to die in the dark, dazed and forwandered, than return to that anguish; he even claimed that he did not know the way. Beleg then admonished Flinding, reminding him of the might, mirth and renown of the Gnomes of Nargothrond. At this, Flinding fought the fear in his heart and started to lead Beleg to the Orc camp.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Lays of Beleriand, "I. The Lay of the Children of Húrin: II. Beleg"
claims.section: section == Other versions of the legendarium == > Lays of Beleriand
